transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Well, doctor, I... I'm here because people just keep acting like I'm imagining it, and it's incredibly frustrating when you know what you're seeing with your own two eyes. I mean, I've been a housekeeper for a long time, so I notice details, you know? I notice when things are out of place or when someone is lingering where they shouldn't be. 

I know for an absolute fact that the hospital people, along with some folks from the agency I get my cleaning jobs through, they've been watching our house. And they don't just watch the house, they've been following my cleaning routes every single day. I'll be carrying my supplies up a client's driveway, maybe three towns over from where I live, and I see them. I can feel them watching me while I'm just trying to get my work done. 

I know exactly why they're doing it, too. They want to see if I'm taking proper care of my husband. Which I am! I work all day scrubbing floors and dusting baseboards, and then I come home and make sure he has everything he needs, but they don't trust me. They think I'm slipping up or neglecting him, so they're coordinating this whole elaborate thing—the hospital and the agency—just to keep tabs on me and catch me doing something wrong. It is exhausting having to look over my shoulder constantly while I'm just trying to mop a floor or take out the trash, knowing they're out there taking notes on me, and then my family has the nerve to tell me it's all in my head...
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people around you do not?

Well, yes, actually. I mean, they say I'm making it up, but I know what I hear. It's usually when I'm finally home from a long day of cleaning, right? I'll have just finished putting away my supplies, the rags are in the wash, and I'm getting dinner ready for my husband. The house will be completely, perfectly quiet. He's usually in the living room watching his programs, and I'll be in the kitchen. 

And then, right by the kitchen window—the one that looks out over the side yard where the rhododendrons are—I hear her. It's a woman's voice. And doctor, it is as clear as a bell. It's not a whisper or a mumble, it's like she's standing right there, maybe just an inch from my ear. She'll tell me things I need to do. She'll say, "Check the back door locks again," or "You need to move his pills to the upper cabinet so they don't find them." 

It's so distinct that the first few times it happened, I actually dropped my dish towel and ran outside to see if one of those agency people had crept up to the window. But there's never anyone there in the bushes. Just the voice. And my husband, he'll yell from the other room asking who I'm talking to, because he can't hear her at all. But she's there, telling me exactly what I need to do to stay ahead of them. It's just so frustrating that nobody else can hear how loud and clear she is.
During the times when you hear the voice or feel people are watching you, have you also been feeling unusually high, energized, or needing much less sleep than usual?

Well, it’s funny you bring up sleep, doctor, because... yes. Yes, I was. There was a stretch just recently, maybe for a few weeks, where I was hardly sleeping at all. I mean, maybe two hours a night? Three if I was lucky? But the strange thing is, I didn't feel tired. Not one bit. I felt... well, I just had this incredible amount of energy, like a motor was running inside my chest and I just had to keep moving. 

I'd be up at 3 AM scrubbing my own baseboards, and then I'd be running—literally rushing—from my morning cleaning jobs straight over to the church. I had all these church errands, you see. I was organizing the donation pantry, and I took it upon myself to polish all the brass in the sanctuary because the regular custodian just does a terrible job, he leaves streaks everywhere. So I was doing my cleaning jobs, doing the church's jobs, just going and going and going...

And that is exactly when it was all happening. During those exact weeks when I was sleeping so little and running from my cleaning jobs to all those church errands, that's when I was seeing those people monitoring my routes the most. I'd be carrying boxes of canned goods into the church hall, buzzing with all this energy, and I'd see their cars parked across the street watching me. And the woman's voice, too! She was right there with me. I'd be polishing a pew at nine o'clock at night, wide awake, and she'd be right in my ear telling me to make sure the side doors were locked so the hospital people couldn't get in to check on my husband. So, yes, all of it—the energy, the not sleeping, the voice, the people watching—it was all happening right at the exact same time.
Have you ever had hallucinations or paranoia when you were not also having that high-energy, little-sleep period?

Well... yes. Yes, actually. I remember there was a spell, just a little while back, where things were much quieter. It lasted for several weeks, I think. I wasn't rushing around at all like I was during that church-cleaning phase. I was actually sleeping quite a bit more—going to bed at a decent hour, maybe around ten o'clock after my husband's shows were over, and sleeping a good, solid seven or eight hours. I felt very calm. Very steady. I wasn't taking on extra errands, just doing my regular day-to-day housekeeping jobs at a normal, sensible pace. 

But the thing is, doctor... even though I was resting and taking it easy, it didn't stop. I still believed—well, I still knew—that the agency was watching us. I'd be driving my usual route, not in any sort of hurry, and I'd still see them keeping tabs on me from down the street. And that voice by the kitchen window? She was still there, too. I'd be having a perfectly quiet evening, just gently washing a couple of dinner plates, feeling completely rested, and she'd still be right there at my shoulder. Telling me to check the locks. 

So it doesn't seem to matter if I'm buzzing with energy or if I'm having a quiet, restful few weeks. They just don't let up. You'd think a person could get a little peace when they're finally getting some sleep, but no, I'll just be standing there looking out at the side yard where the rhododendrons are, feeling perfectly fine, and she'll start right up again about how they're coming to check on my husband...
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing or seeing things or feeling watched, but you were not having the high-energy, little-sleep symptoms?

Well, like I was just trying to explain a moment ago, doctor—maybe I didn't make the timeline clear enough, I know I tend to get a bit ahead of myself when I'm talking—but yes, absolutely. It was definitely for at least two weeks. Honestly, it was probably closer to three or four weeks of that very quiet spell I just mentioned. 

I wasn't rushing around at all during that time. I was sleeping perfectly fine, getting my solid seven or eight hours, going to bed right after my husband's television programs ended, usually right around ten o'clock. My energy was completely normal. I wasn't doing any of those extra church errands, I was just pacing myself through my regular housekeeping jobs. I remember I was cleaning Mrs. Gable's house on Tuesdays and Thursdays during that stretch, just taking my time dusting her antique furniture, not feeling that motor running in my chest at all. I felt completely steady.

But even during those several weeks, when I was so well-rested and calm... the agency didn't stop watching us. I'd still see their vehicles parked down the street from the houses I was cleaning, keeping tabs on my routes. And that woman's voice by the kitchen window, right by the rhododendrons like I told you, she was still there just the same. I'd be standing there at the sink, completely rested, feeling perfectly fine, and she'd still be right at my shoulder telling me to check the locks and make sure they weren't coming for my husband. 

So, yes, it definitely went on for several weeks where I was sleeping more and didn't have any of that extra rushing energy, but the voice and the people watching me were still happening every single day. They just never take a vacation, doctor, even when my body is finally getting some proper rest.
Have there ever been times when you were hearing voices or feeling watched even though you were not having any mood episode at all, like not feeling depressed or unusually energized?

Well, doctor, I feel like we might be going in circles just a little bit, because that's exactly what I've been trying to tell you about that quieter spell. During those several weeks I just mentioned, I wasn't just... well, I wasn't just not energized. I wasn't depressed or down in the dumps either. I wasn't crying or staying in bed or feeling gloomy, nothing like that at all. 

My mood was just perfectly normal. Just regular, everyday me. I'd get up in the morning, have my coffee with a little bit of cream, gather up my cleaning supplies, and go do my housekeeping jobs without rushing around. And then I'd come home and cook dinner, maybe a nice meatloaf or some chicken, and sit with my husband. I was sleeping more, getting my full rest like I said, and just taking life at a very even, steady pace. No high highs, no low lows. Just a completely normal, average few weeks.

But even then—even without feeling overly happy or overly sad, just feeling completely level—it was all still happening. I'd be right there at the kitchen window, washing the dinner dishes, looking out at the side yard, feeling completely fine and calm, but I still heard her voice clear as a bell right there with me. And I still knew, without a shadow of a doubt, that the agency was out there watching our house and keeping tabs on my routes. So yes, even when my mood is completely fine and steady and I'm not having any sort of episode with my energy or my sadness, the voice and the watching... they don't go away. They just stay right there with me.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest in things nearly every day?

Depressed? Lost interest in things? No... no, I really can't say that I have. I mean, goodness, everyone has a morning here or there where they look out the window at the rain and think, 'Oh, I'd rather just stay under the quilt today,' but to feel like that every single day for two whole weeks? No, absolutely not. 

I've just never been that kind of person. I'm a doer, doctor. Even when things are perfectly quiet and steady, or even when that woman by the window is chattering away at me and the agency is parking their cars down the street, I still get up and I still care about my work. I take a lot of pride in my housekeeping, you know. You can't just lose interest when people are relying on you. Like with Mrs. Gable—I mentioned I clean for her on Tuesdays and Thursdays—she has these beautiful antique side tables in her front room, real cherry wood, very delicate, and you have to use a specific oil on them. You can't just stop caring about those details, or you'll ruin the finish! And my husband, well, he needs his dinners. He works hard, and he expects a nice hot meal when he gets home. 

I've never had a time where I was so down in the dumps or gloomy that I stopped wanting to cook for him or stopped wanting to keep our house nice. I might get a little too revved up sometimes, like that church-cleaning phase I told you about, or I might just be my regular, steady self, but I've never had a spell where I just felt depressed and gave up on my life for weeks on end. I always keep my routines going. That's just never happened to me.
Have there been any times when the voice or the feeling that people were watching you happened only while you were having the high-energy, little-sleep periods, and not at other times?

Well, no, not *only* during those times, because like I was just saying, I hear her and see them even when I'm perfectly calm. But yes, it definitely happens *during* those high-energy times too. Oh, absolutely it does. 

In fact, I remember very clearly, during that stretch I was telling you about—you know, the one where I was sleeping maybe two or three hours a night and just bouncing out of bed before the sun was even thinking about coming up, rushing off to do my regular housekeeping jobs and then heading straight over to the church to polish all the brass and wash down the pews until late in the evening. Well, during those weeks, when my motor was just running and running and running, the voice was right there with me. I'd be at the church, scrubbing the baseboards in the fellowship hall, moving so fast, and that woman's voice would be right there, telling me to check the windows, telling me they were coming. 

And the agency, well, they were definitely still watching me then, too. I'd be zipping from Mrs. Gable's house over to the church, just full of energy, and I'd see those same vehicles parked near the intersections, keeping track of my routes. I remember thinking they must be having a hard time keeping up with me because I was moving so quickly from place to place! So, yes, it definitely happens when I'm all revved up and not sleeping, but it's not *only* then. Like I said, it happens when I'm calm and steady, too. It just seems like no matter how much energy I have, whether I'm rushing around like a whirlwind or just taking my time dusting, they never, ever leave me alone.
